message.content:
You are auditing a Polymarket paper-trading bot at /home/user/JSF before its LIVE launch. Real money will follow this code. Your job is to find what is actually wrong, not to bless it and not to invent problems.

SYSTEM UNDER AUDIT
- Trades 5-minute and 15-minute crypto Up/Down binary markets on Polymarket for btc, eth, sol, xrp, doge. One process per coin: python3 bot/run.py --coin <c>. Deployed on a DigitalOcean Amsterdam droplet via systemd (deploy/droplet_setup.sh, jsf-paperbot@.service template, jsf.slice memory limits).
- VERIFIED CONTRACT (settlement rule, post 2026-08-07): Up wins iff mean(P over [t1-w, t1)) >= mean(P over [t0-w, t0)), where t0/t1 are the market open/close boundary timestamps, w=30s for 5m markets and w=60s for 15m markets, and P is the Chainlink real-time price stream (RTDS websocket ticks, ms timestamps). This reading was verified on thousands of settled markets (0.95 agreement vs 0.89 for alternatives).
- STRATEGY (bot/strategy.py, RollAvgEdge): once inside the final window, S = sum of observed oracle ticks in [t1-w, now), K = mean over [t0-w, t0), spot = latest oracle price, rem = t1 - now. z = (S + rem*spot - w*K) / (sigma * sqrt(rem^3/3)). Buy Up when z >= 2 and ask <= 0.99; buy Down when z <= -2. Gate: only trades when rem <= min(window_s=60, w) -- so 5m markets trade only in their last 30s, 15m in their last 60s; min_rem_s=2.0 floor. sigma comes from the oracle tick stream (state.py sigma_rel), Binance 1s klines are a guarded fallback.
- VENUE FACTS (as currently believed -- config.json): 250ms mandatory taker hold on crypto up/down (venue_hold_ms) plus measured network rtt_ms; taker fee 0.07*p*(1-p) per share; orderMinSize=5 shares; tick 0.01; FAK order type. Paper fills simulate: cap = min(order budget, displayed book depth at limit * participation 0.5, shares PRINTED at the limit in last 5s * 0.25), reject_rate 1%, and consume() decrements displayed size so repeated fires cannot re-eat the same displayed shares.
- RESULTS SO FAR: paper run +4.55c/share on 536 markets (t=+4.13, ~$2.4k booked at 100sh/market cap). Offline tape benchmark ~+1.8c/share; the gap is attributed to the tape pricing z off Binance while the venue settles off Chainlink (reports/findings.md section 9.6).
- A prior adversarial audit already ran (findings.md sections 9.x): known fixed issues include the 250ms hold being added, participation caps, the sigma fallback guard, fair_legacy removal, restart verification, per-coin logs. Do not re-report those as new findings; DO report if a supposed fix is incomplete or wrong.

RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
- READ the assigned files COMPLETELY, line by line. Do not skim. Quote exact lines (file:line) as evidence for every finding.
- You may run read-only commands (python3 snippets, grep) to test a hypothesis against the code or the local data. Do NOT modify any file, do NOT run the bot, do NOT touch anything under deploy/ as a command.
- Severity: fatal = would lose money or invalidate the paper result; major = materially wrong number, unsafe on restart/error, or launch blocker; minor = wrong but low consequence; improvement = concrete profitable idea, not a defect.
- No style nits, no docstring complaints, no "consider adding tests" filler. Every finding must state a concrete failure scenario or a concrete profit improvement with numbers where possible.
- If you find NOTHING real in an area, say so -- an empty findings list from a hard look is a valid result.

You are the adversarial VERIFIER for the 'accounting' reviewer. Findings claimed (JSON):
[
 {
  "title": "Whole 536-market headline record predates the double-dip ledger; re-claims included",
  "file": "src/audit_doubledip.py",
  "line": 5,
  "severity": "major",
  "claim": "The +4.55c/share / $2.4k / 536-market record the launch rests on was produced entirely by the pre-9fbc1bc broker that could re-eat the same displayed liquidity after every book refresh, and neither score_paper nor status excludes or down-weights the possible re-claims; the fill-model-change reset policy (deploy/reset_pnl.sh) was not applied at 9fbc1bc.",
  "evidence": "src/audit_doubledip.py:5-7: \"The fills already on disk were taken WITHOUT that ledger, so the same displayed ask could be re-eaten after every venue book refresh\". bot/run.py:690-692: \"so without a lifetime ledger the same displayed liquidity can be eaten several times per market. This is the binding realism cap.\" Git dates: record reset bfb8024 2026-08-11 09:43; ledger fix 9fbc1bc 2026-08-12 10:24; the 9.6 aggregate quoting live 4.55c was committed edd3489 2026-08-12 10:18 — i.e. 100% of the quoted record is pre-ledger. deploy/reset_pnl.sh:8-9: \"Mixing them into the same log means the scorer averages two incompatible fill models\" — yet no reset accompanied 9fbc1bc.",
  "failure_scenario": "If audit_doubledip's flagged fraction on the droplet is, say, 25% of shares, then booked P&L (~$2.4k), shares/market, and every $/day projection overstate deployable capacity by roughly that fraction — the live bot, running the ledger, will simply not get those fills. c/share and the market-clustered t are less exposed (re-claims fill at the same price in the same market), but total-$ tracking vs the $2,100/day projection will read as live underperformance that is actually paper over-crediting. Launch sizing calibrated on the blended record is calibrated on phantom liquidity.",
  "fix": "Before go-live, run src/audit_doubledip.py on the droplet and make the 'clean' (first-claims-only) subset the launch decision number; either run deploy/reset_pnl.sh to start a post-ledger record, or add the re-claim flag as a default exclusion in score_paper/status so the headline is the ledger-consistent one."
 },
 {
  "title": "Clustered t assumes same-window markets independent; t=+4.13 is an upper bound",
  "file": "src/status.py",
  "line": 108,
  "severity": "major",
  "claim": "The headline t clusters on slug only, but the five coins' 5m markets in the SAME window settle on the same crypto-wide move (measured up_win correlation 0.52-0.65 across coins on 234k local settled markets), and at every :15 boundary a coin's 5m and 15m markets close together (67% outcome agreement). Five bots firing on one market-wide move are ~one bet, not five, so the market-clustered SE is understated and t=+4.13 overstated.",
  "evidence": "src/status.py:101-109: g = sc.groupby(\"slug\")... print(f\"t = {tcl:+.2f} clustered by market (n={len(g)} markets...\"); src/score_paper.py:251: \"clustered by market (n={len(g)} markets)   <- the honest one\"; src/tape_capacity.py:113-114 even mislabels the same slug-clustering as \"t(day-clustered by market...)\" though nothing clusters by day. Measured on data/pmfree_aug/meta (234,317 settled markets): cross-coin same-t1 5m up_win correlations btc-eth 0.653, btc-sol 0.585, btc-xrp 0.551, btc-doge 0.515; every 5m window lists all five coins; same-coin same-close 5m vs 15m agreement 0.6717 on n=4,359.",
  "failure_scenario": "z fires when the final-window drift is large, which is disproportionately a market-wide move, so co-firing across coins is common. If ~30% of the 536 markets share their close window with one other traded market at outcome correlation ~0.57, the SE is understated ~8% (t 4.13 -> ~3.8); in the regime where all five coins co-fire on the same windows the cluster-sum variance inflates by (1+4*0.57) and t 4.13 -> ~2.3. The launch stat could sit anywhere in 2.3-3.8 instead of 4.13, and nothing in the code can tell you which.",
  "fix": "Cluster on the close boundary: key = the t1 epoch in the slug (pooling coins and 5m/15m that share a close), or at minimum (t1, coin). Apply the same key in score_paper._report, status.pnl_by_bot and tape_capacity.clustered_t, and fix the false \"day-clustered\" label in tape_capacity.py:114."
 },
 {
  "title": "Maker fills invisible to default scoring and mis-charged a taker fee when included",
  "file": "src/score_paper.py",
  "line": 192,
  "severity": "minor",
  "claim": "paper.py books maker fills with no fee and emits them with no meta, so score_paper's default filters silently exclude every maker fill (empty reason fails reason_prefix, missing seen_px fails the latency filter, missing oracle_age_s fails the oracle filter), and when forced in with --reason-prefix '' --all-latency --all-oracle they are charged the taker fee they never paid via the fee_per_sh fallback.",
  "evidence": "bot/paper.py:111-113: pos[\"cost\"] += fill * o[\"level\"] ... self._emit(\"maker_fill\", oid=..., px=o[\"level\"], shares=fill) — no fee, no meta. src/score_paper.py:148-156: reason/seen_px/oracle_age filters all read meta, which is {} for maker fills. src/score_paper.py:192: fee = float(f.get(\"fee_per_sh\", FEE * px * (1 - px))) — fallback applies the taker formula to maker fills.",
  "failure_scenario": "Currently latent (RollAvgEdge emits only taker_buy: bot/strategy.py:295,307; the maker strategies are disabled in config). But the day GzValueMaker/VacuumLadder or a rollavg maker variant is enabled, its entire P&L is invisible in the default status/score_paper headline — a maker strategy bleeding money would not appear anywhere — and any manual widened scoring mis-books it by 0.07*p*(1-p) (up to 1.75c/share near p=0.5) per fill.",
  "fix": "Emit maker fills with meta (reason, oracle_age_s) and fee_per_sh=0.0 in paper.py, and make score_rows use fee_per_sh=0 for kind==maker_fill instead of the taker fallback."
 },
 {
  "title": "A voided/50-50 resolution is booked as Up total loss and Down total win",
  "file": "src/score_paper.py",
  "line": 64,
  "severity": "minor",
  "claim": "outcomes_for maps outcomePrices to a boolean with float(op[iu]) > 0.5, so a market the venue resolves 50/50 (refund at $0.50/share, the standard remedy for an oracle outage on these series) is booked as Up lost / Down won: Up fills take -px-fee instead of +0.50-px-fee, and Down fills take +1-px-fee instead of +0.50-px-fee.",
  "evidence": "src/score_paper.py:64: out[m[\"slug\"]] = float(op[iu]) > 0.5. Same test in the bot's own settlement fallback, bot/run.py:545: return 0 if float(op[iu]) > 0.5 else 1 — which additionally feeds risk.day_pnl and the kill switch.",
  "failure_scenario": "A Chainlink stream outage voids a batch of 5m markets 50/50. A bot holding ~100 shares of Up at 0.97 in each is booked -97c/share when the true outcome is -47c/share; a Down holder is booked +2c when the truth is -47c. The record and day_pnl both mis-book by ~0.50/share in whichever direction, and the kill switch can trip (or fail to trip) on fictional numbers. Zero 50/50 outcomes observed in 234,317 local settled markets, so this is tail risk, not a current distortion.",
  "fix": "Treat outcomePrices where max(op) < 0.99 as a distinct 'voided' status: book pnl = sh*(0.5 - px - fee) (fee treatment per venue refund policy) and count it separately in the report; same guard in run.py _gamma_result."
 },
 {
  "title": "No fill dedup key or fill-model stamp; record integrity rests on manual archiving",
  "file": "src/score_paper.py",
  "line": 119,
  "severity": "minor",
  "claim": "gather() concatenates logs/*/paper_fills.jsonl plus the legacy flat log with no per-fill identity (no dedup on slug/t_us/oid) and no broker-version stamp, so (a) any duplicated or restored file double-counts fills undetected, and (b) fills from the pre-0ca2161 broker (96% price-reach, 100% displayed size) pass every default filter — they carry seen_px and oracle_age_s — and are excluded from the headline only because deploy/reset_pnl.sh was manually run on 2026-08-11; the code cannot tell the eras apart.",
  "evidence": "src/score_paper.py:119-121: logs = sorted(glob.glob(\"logs/*/paper_fills.jsonl\")); if os.path.exists(\"logs/paper_fills.jsonl\"): logs.append(...) — then lines 131-139 append every taker/maker fill line with no key. deploy/reset_pnl.sh:4-9: \"Every fill before 0ca2161 was produced by a broker that reached its price 96% of the time... Mixing them into the same log means the scorer averages two incompatible fill models\". Git: latency stamps default 53e1737 (Aug 11 06:13) predates the fill-mechanics rewrite 0ca2161 (09:38), so a multi-hour band of fills passes all default filters yet used the fictional broker.",
  "failure_scenario": "An operator restores an archive (cp logs/archive/<stamp>/btc/paper_fills.jsonl logs/btc/ to 'look at old data'), or runs score_paper on a host where reset_pnl was never executed: the pre-cap fills silently blend into and inflate the headline c/share with no warning — exactly the 'meaningless blend' the reset script exists to prevent — or identical duplicated lines double every affected fill's weight.",
  "fix": "Stamp meta with a fill_model version (bump at every broker-mechanics change) in paper.py._emit and default-filter score_paper to the current version; drop exact-duplicate (slug, side, t_us, px, shares) lines with a loud count when they appear."
 },
 {
  "title": "reset_pnl.sh: bot for a coin dropped from config keeps writing into the archive",
  "file": "deploy/reset_pnl.sh",
  "line": 24,
  "severity": "minor",
  "claim": "The stop list is derived from the CURRENT bot/config.json coins, so a still-running unit for a coin since removed from config is never stopped; its open append fd follows the mv, so after the reset it keeps appending new fills into logs/archive/<stamp>/<coin>/paper_fills.jsonl — the live record silently loses that coin's fills and the archive gains post-reset fills, blending eras inside the archive. Separately, the final loop starts every configured unit unconditionally, including bots an operator had deliberately stopped.",
  "evidence": "deploy/reset_pnl.sh:24-26: COINS=$(python3 -c \"...get('coins',['btc'])\"); UNITS=$(for c in $COINS; ...) — only these are stopped; line 36: mv \"$src\" \"$DEST/${src#logs/}\" (a running writer's fd follows the inode); lines 41-43: for u in $UNITS; do systemctl start \"$u\" ... — unconditional start.",
  "failure_scenario": "Operator drops doge from config.json (edge went negative) but forgets to stop jsf-paperbot@doge, then runs reset_pnl.sh: doge trades on with all its fills landing in the archive — invisible to status.py/score_paper (glob depth excludes archive) — so a losing bot runs unmonitored indefinitely. Or: xrp was stopped pending its inverted-gap investigation; a routine paper reset restarts it. Live, that is unsupervised real-money trading.",
  "fix": "Derive UNITS from running units (systemctl list-units 'jsf-paperbot@*') as well as config; record which units were active before stopping and start only those; after archiving, assert no process holds the archived files open (lsof)."
 }
]

For EACH finding: open the cited file at the cited lines, re-derive the claim from the actual code, and try to REFUTE it. A finding is CONFIRMED only if the quoted code really does what the claim says and the failure scenario is reachable. REFUTED needs the specific code fact that kills it (e.g. a guard the reviewer missed elsewhere -- search the repo for it). UNCERTAIN only when deciding needs data/runtime you cannot access. For 'improvement' findings, CONFIRMED means the improvement is real and the sizing plausible. Run read-only python3/grep to check numeric claims where possible. Do not modify files. Keep the 'title' field EXACTLY as given so verdicts can be joined back to findings.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
